temaNombre: Plants: roots, stems, leaves and flowers
title: Discovering plant parts
summary: Learn to recognise roots, stems, leaves and flowers.
keyIdeas: Roots hold plants in the soil and take in water.
Stems support plants and carry water.

basicKnowledge: A. Cultura científica › La vida en nuestro planeta

activities.prompt: Which plant part usually grows hidden underground?
activities.explanation: Roots usually grow underground and hold the plant in the soil.
activities.hint: It grows down to reach water.

activities.prompt: Match each plant part to its main job.
activities.explanation: Each plant part has a job that helps it live and reproduce.

activities.prompt: The stem carries water from the roots to the leaves.
activities.explanation: The stem carries water around the plant, a little like a drinking straw.

activities.prompt: Sort plant parts and things plants need.
activities.explanation: Roots, stems and flowers are plant parts. Plants need water, light and air.

activities.prompt: Complete the sentence with the right plant part.
activities.explanation: Roots absorb water from the soil.
activities.sentence: The ___ absorbs water from the soil.

activities.prompt: Aisha puts a plant in a cupboard with no light. What will happen?
activities.explanation: Green plants need light to make food and grow well.
activities.hint: Leaves need light to make food.
options: It will grow greener and stronger
It will grow lots of colourful flowers
It will become yellow and weak

activities.prompt: Put the growth of a bean plant in order.
activities.explanation: When the seed germinates, a root appears first, then the stem and leaves. Flowers appear later.

activities.prompt: Omar says, 'Plants drink water through their flowers.' Why is he wrong?
activities.explanation: Plants take water from soil through their roots, rather than through flowers.
activities.hint: Think about where you water a potted plant.
options: They take water from the soil through their roots
They take water from the air through branches

activities.prompt: All plant leaves have the same shape.
activities.explanation: Leaves have many shapes: long, round or needle-shaped, like pine needles.

activities.prompt: Read about Mateo's experiment and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: The stem carries water and nutrients to the plant's upper parts.
activities.title: The carnation experiment
activities.text: With an adult's help, Mateo puts a white carnation in water with red food colouring. The next day, its white petals have red patches. The water has travelled up the stem to the flower.

questions.prompt: Through which plant part did the coloured water travel?
questions.explanation: The stem carries water from the glass to the petals.

questions.prompt: Which part of the carnation had red patches?
questions.explanation: The coloured water reached the flower and coloured its petals.
